prompt: rgb.jpg is a horizontal strip of 5 frames, left to right in time order, sampled from the few seconds of a head-mounted (egocentric) video; the camera wearer is the viewpoint. depth.jpg, segmentation.jpg and pose.jpg are the same 5 frames rendered as a monocular depth map (brighter = nearer to the camera wearer), an instance segmentation map (coloured masks with class labels), and a body/hand skeleton map (yellow = body, magenta = hands) on black. Look at all four images. For EACH of the three maps, describe the spatial understanding that map supports, using the RGB strip for context: the layout of the scene; which people and objects are present and roughly how far each is from the camera wearer (in metres) and from each other; relative positions (left/right/in front/behind, above/below); which way people face and whether they look toward the camera wearer; what is within arm's reach of the camera wearer or of others; occlusions and anything partly out of view; and how these change across the 5 frames (approach, retreat, turning). Say what each map shows that is hard to see in the RGB alone, and where the map looks unreliable. Describe only spatial facts. Do not guess anyone's intentions, social norms, or what anyone should do. Return only JSON: {"depth": "...", "segmentation": "...", "pose": "..."} with 3-5 sentences each.

descriptions.depth: The depth map shows a narrow indoor room with a vertical wall on the right (0.3 to 1.5 m away, brightest on the right edge) and a floor sloping downward and away to a doorway at the top (about 2.0 to 2.5 m ahead). The camera wearer's hands and torso at the bottom (0.2 to 0.5 m) grip the near end of an elongated wooden cabinet (extending from 0.4 m to 2.0 m in front and slightly right) that has three internal compartments and a rectangular metal insert in the nearest compartment. A second person stands near the top-left doorway about 2.0 to 2.5 m from the camera wearer and 0.3 to 0.8 m left of the far end of the cabinet, initially holding a broom and dustpan within their arm's reach before setting the broom against the left wall in frame 4 and stepping right to grasp the far end of the cabinet in frame 5, where the cabinet partially occludes their lower legs. Across the 5 frames, the cabinet rotates slightly counterclockwise to align parallel with the right wall while the second person's torso (partly out of view above the top frame edge) turns from facing right and downward to facing toward the cabinet and the camera wearer. Compared to RGB alone, the depth gradient clearly separates the elevated top rim of the cabinet from its recessed compartments and shows the continuous foreshortening of the right wall, though it is unreliable in the dark upper-left floor region where the broom handle, dustpan, and doorway threshold fade into near-black background values.
descriptions.segmentation: The instance segmentation map isolates two people in the scene: the camera wearer's arms, hands, and lower torso at the bottom edge (0.2 to 0.5 m away) and the second person at the top edge (2.0 to 2.5 m ahead in front and to the left), separated by roughly 1.5 to 2.0 m along the length of the wooden cabinet between them. Across the 5 frames, the upper person's mask shifts from the top-left (where they face right with a dustpan and broom in arm's reach in frames 1 to 3) toward the top-center in frames 4 and 5 as they turn to face the camera wearer and reach both hands down onto the far end of the cabinet, with their head and upper chest cropped out of view at the top border. While segmentation sharply delineates the silhouette of the camera wearer's forearms gripping the near cabinet edge and tracks the distant person's legs and arms against the cluttered floor, it completely fails to segment the wooden cabinet, the walls, the doors on the left, or the broom. The map is also unreliable in its class labels and instance consistency: in frame 1 it splits the camera wearer's left and right arms into two separate 'person' instances (brown and cyan), in frame 2 it misclassifies the rectangular metal insert inside the near cabinet compartment (0.6 m away) as a green 'laptop', in frame 4 it places a stray 'person' label in empty mid-frame space, and in frame 5 it clips the camera wearer's right hand.
descriptions.pose: The pose map is almost entirely blank across the 5 frames, detecting only a partial yellow body skeleton for the second person in the top-left corner of frame 1 (roughly 2.2 m in front of and to the left of the camera wearer) and nothing in frames 2 through 5. In frame 1, the sparse keypoints locate the second person's right arm reaching down and left toward the dustpan (within their arm's reach at about 2.3 m from the camera wearer) and one leg standing on the floor to the left of the wooden cabinet, with their head occluded by the top frame boundary and no gaze or facial orientation keypoints visible. This single skeleton provides a rough 2D joint axis for the person's bent posture in frame 1 that simplifies the cluttered background in the RGB image. However, the map is highly unreliable overall because steep egocentric foreshortening and top-edge cropping cause total detection failure for the second person's movement, turning, and cabinet grasping across frames 2 to 5, as well as complete omission of the camera wearer's own hands and arms at the bottom of the frame (0.2 to 0.5 m away) throughout the entire sequence.
